slowest_experiments.experiment: V602 evidence, substrate, and executable-manifest contract
Text-anchored relation and bounded ASP atom fixture

summary: The milestone closed two experiments in 0.2 minutes; one carried the compute-bound marker. V602 evidence, substrate, and executable-manifest contract forms the compute critical path, while the supplied evidence does not break its interval into stages.
bottlenecks_identified: Artifact modification times collapse all work inside the compute task into one interval, which leaves its duration unexplained.
The accelerator report is a point-in-time snapshot with no experiment ownership, so it cannot quantify compute-task utilization.
No launch record captures model concurrency or dispatcher choice, which makes the DualGPURunner check indeterminate.
improvements_suggested: Write monotonic timestamps at the start and finish of each harness stage.
Sample accelerator load under the experiment process and store those samples with the result.
Persist model concurrency, selected runner, and dispatch reason in launch metadata; reserve DualGPURunner for parallel multi-model work.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add monotonic phase timing to the experiment harness.
Write task-owned accelerator samples into each compute artifact.
Record model concurrency and runner selection at launch.
meta_reflection: This record supports an observability change, not a measured speedup claim. One task-scoped launch receipt can expose stage cost, accelerator engagement, and dispatcher selection in the next milestone.
